name: Web apps
description: Everything that goes into software delivered through a browser

categories.name: Rendering & architecture
categories.description: Where the HTML is put together, and how much of the app the browser has to run.

subcategories.name: Single-page apps
subcategories.description: Loads the shell once, then rewrites the page in place as the reader navigates.

subcategories.name: Multi-page apps
subcategories.description: Asks the server for a fresh document on every navigation.

subcategories.name: Server-side rendering
subcategories.description: Builds the HTML per request, then hands the page to the client framework to take over.

subcategories.name: Static site generation
subcategories.description: Renders every page at build time, so nothing has to run when a reader arrives.

subcategories.name: Islands & partial hydration
subcategories.description: Ships static HTML and boots JavaScript only for the few parts that are interactive.

subcategories.name: Progressive web apps
subcategories.description: Installs to the home screen, works offline, and behaves like a native app.

subcategories.name: Edge rendering
subcategories.description: Runs the render close to the reader on a CDN node instead of in one origin region.

categories.name: Frontend frameworks
categories.description: The libraries that turn application state into what the reader actually sees.

subcategories.name: Component frameworks
subcategories.description: Describe the interface as components, and let the framework keep the DOM in step.

subcategories.name: Compile-time frameworks
subcategories.description: Do the reactivity work at build time so less framework code ships to the browser.

subcategories.name: Meta-frameworks
subcategories.description: Bundle routing, data loading, and a server into an opinionated full-stack package.

subcategories.name: HTML over the wire
subcategories.description: Sends rendered fragments from the server and swaps them in, skipping the client model entirely.

subcategories.name: Web components
subcategories.description: Custom elements that work in any framework, or none, because the browser owns them.

categories.name: Styling & UI systems
categories.description: How a web app gets its look, and how that look stays consistent across a team.

subcategories.name: Utility CSS
subcategories.description: Composes styles from small single-purpose classes written in the markup.

subcategories.name: CSS-in-JS
subcategories.description: Declares styles in JavaScript, scoped to the component that uses them.

subcategories.name: Preprocessors & tooling
subcategories.description: Extends plain CSS with variables, nesting, and build-time transforms.

subcategories.name: Component libraries
subcategories.description: Ready-made buttons, dialogs, and tables with styling already decided.

subcategories.name: Headless primitives
subcategories.description: Accessible behaviour for menus, dialogs, and comboboxes with no styling attached.

subcategories.name: Design tokens
subcategories.description: One source of truth for colour, spacing, and type, shared by design and code.

categories.name: Client state & routing
categories.description: Keeping track of what the app knows and where in the app the reader is.

subcategories.name: State stores
subcategories.description: Holds application state outside the component tree so any screen can read it.

subcategories.name: Server-state caching
subcategories.description: Fetches, caches, and revalidates server data so screens stay fresh without manual plumbing.

subcategories.name: Client routing
subcategories.description: Maps URLs to views and handles navigation without a full page load.

subcategories.name: Forms & validation
subcategories.description: Tracks field state and checks input against a schema before it reaches the server.

subcategories.name: Client storage
subcategories.description: Keeps data in the browser between visits, from a single flag to a whole local database.

categories.name: APIs & data transport
categories.description: The contract between the browser and everything behind it.

subcategories.name: REST
subcategories.description: Resources addressed by URL and manipulated with HTTP verbs.

subcategories.name: GraphQL
subcategories.description: One endpoint where the client asks for exactly the fields it needs.

subcategories.name: RPC
subcategories.description: Calls a remote function as if it were local, with the types checked end to end.

subcategories.name: Webhooks & events
subcategories.description: The server calls you when something happens, instead of being polled.

subcategories.name: API gateways
subcategories.description: One front door that routes, authenticates, and rate-limits traffic to many services.

subcategories.name: Schemas & documentation
subcategories.description: Describes an API formally, so clients, docs, and mocks can be generated from it.

categories.name: Server frameworks & runtimes
categories.description: The code that answers the request once it leaves the browser.

subcategories.name: JavaScript runtimes
subcategories.description: Runs JavaScript or TypeScript on the server side of the app.

subcategories.name: JavaScript frameworks
subcategories.description: Routing, middleware, and request handling for a JavaScript server.

subcategories.name: Python frameworks
subcategories.description: From batteries-included stacks to thin async APIs.

subcategories.name: Ruby & PHP frameworks
subcategories.description: The convention-over-configuration tradition that shaped modern web frameworks.

subcategories.name: JVM & .NET frameworks
subcategories.description: Statically typed stacks built for long-lived enterprise services.

subcategories.name: Go & Rust frameworks
subcategories.description: Compiled servers chosen when throughput and memory footprint matter.

categories.name: Realtime & collaboration
categories.description: Apps where the screen changes because someone else did something.

subcategories.name: WebSockets
subcategories.description: A two-way connection held open between browser and server.

subcategories.name: Server-sent events
subcategories.description: A one-way stream from server to browser over ordinary HTTP.

subcategories.name: WebRTC
subcategories.description: Peer-to-peer audio, video, and data straight between two browsers.

subcategories.name: Hosted pub/sub
subcategories.description: Someone else runs the socket fleet and you publish to channels.

subcategories.name: Collaborative editing
subcategories.description: Merges concurrent edits from many people without a central lock.

categories.name: Auth & identity
categories.description: Proving who someone is, then deciding what they may do.

subcategories.name: Sessions & cookies
subcategories.description: The server remembers the login and hands the browser an opaque ticket.

subcategories.name: Tokens & standards
subcategories.description: Signed credentials that travel with the request instead of living on the server.

subcategories.name: Identity providers
subcategories.description: Hosted login, signup, and account management you drop into an app.

subcategories.name: Enterprise SSO
subcategories.description: One corporate identity signs into every internal and vendor app.

subcategories.name: Passwordless & passkeys
subcategories.description: Logs in with a device key or an emailed link, with no password to steal.

subcategories.name: Authorization
subcategories.description: Decides, per request, whether this identity may touch this resource.

categories.name: Databases & persistence
categories.description: Where the app's data actually lives once the request is over.

subcategories.name: Relational databases
subcategories.description: Tables, joins, and transactions, still the default for most web apps.

subcategories.name: Document & key-value stores
subcategories.description: Schemaless documents or plain keys, tuned for scale over joins.

subcategories.name: ORMs & query builders
subcategories.description: Maps rows to objects, or composes SQL without string concatenation.

subcategories.name: Search engines
subcategories.description: Full-text and faceted search that a LIKE query cannot do well.

subcategories.name: Caching layers
subcategories.description: Keeps hot results close to the request so the database is asked less often.

subcategories.name: Object & file storage
subcategories.description: Holds the uploads, images, and exports that do not belong in a database.

categories.name: Build tooling
categories.description: Everything between the source you write and the files a browser downloads.

subcategories.name: Bundlers
subcategories.description: Resolves the module graph and emits the assets the page loads.

subcategories.name: Compilers & transpilers
subcategories.description: Turns modern or typed source into JavaScript every target browser understands.

subcategories.name: Package managers
subcategories.description: Installs dependencies and pins them so every machine builds the same tree.

subcategories.name: Monorepo tooling
subcategories.description: Runs and caches tasks across many packages in one repository.

subcategories.name: Linting & formatting
subcategories.description: Catches mistakes and settles style arguments before review does.

categories.name: Testing
categories.description: Checking the app behaves, at every level from a function to a whole browser.

subcategories.name: Unit testing
subcategories.description: Exercises one function or module in isolation.

subcategories.name: Component testing
subcategories.description: Renders a component and interacts with it the way a reader would.

subcategories.name: End-to-end testing
subcategories.description: Drives a real browser through a whole user journey.

subcategories.name: Visual regression
subcategories.description: Screenshots the UI and flags pixels that changed without permission.

subcategories.name: Load & stress testing
subcategories.description: Finds where the app falls over before real traffic does.

subcategories.name: Accessibility testing
subcategories.description: Automated checks for the barriers a keyboard or screen reader would hit.

categories.name: Hosting & delivery
categories.description: Getting the app onto machines the public can reach, repeatedly and safely.

subcategories.name: Application platforms
subcategories.description: Push a repository and the platform builds, deploys, and scales it.

subcategories.name: Containers & orchestration
subcategories.description: Ships the app with its environment, then schedules copies across a cluster.

subcategories.name: Serverless functions
subcategories.description: Runs a handler per request with no server to keep alive.

subcategories.name: CDNs & edge networks
subcategories.description: Caches and serves assets from the point of presence nearest the reader.

subcategories.name: CI/CD
subcategories.description: Builds, tests, and releases on every push without anyone running commands.

subcategories.name: Infrastructure as code
subcategories.description: Declares the servers, buckets, and DNS in files that live in version control.

categories.name: Performance
categories.description: How quickly the page becomes useful, and how it feels once it is.

subcategories.name: Core Web Vitals
subcategories.description: The field metrics that stand in for loading, responsiveness, and layout stability.

subcategories.name: Payload optimization
subcategories.description: Ships less JavaScript, and smaller images, to begin with.

subcategories.name: Caching strategies
subcategories.description: Decides what may be reused, for how long, and who is allowed to serve it.

subcategories.name: Profiling tools
subcategories.description: Measures a real page instead of guessing at what is slow.

categories.name: Monitoring & analytics
categories.description: Knowing what the app did in production, and what people did with it.

subcategories.name: Error tracking
subcategories.description: Collects exceptions with the stack trace and context needed to fix them.

subcategories.name: Real user monitoring
subcategories.description: Measures performance on the devices and networks readers actually have.

subcategories.name: Product analytics
subcategories.description: Tracks funnels, retention, and which features get used.

subcategories.name: Logging & tracing
subcategories.description: Follows one request across every service it touches.

subcategories.name: Session replay
subcategories.description: Reconstructs what a reader saw and clicked when something went wrong.

categories.name: Web security
categories.description: The attacks a public web app invites, and the defences that answer them.

subcategories.name: Injection & XSS
subcategories.description: Stops attacker input being executed as code or SQL.

subcategories.name: CSRF & clickjacking
subcategories.description: Stops another site making requests, or drawing over yours.

subcategories.name: Transport security
subcategories.description: Encrypts traffic and makes downgrading to plaintext impossible.

subcategories.name: Dependencies & secrets
subcategories.description: Watches the supply chain, and keeps credentials out of the repository.

subcategories.name: Abuse & bot defence
subcategories.description: Keeps scrapers, credential stuffing, and floods away from the origin.

subcategories.name: Standards & audits
subcategories.description: Checks the app against a published list of what usually goes wrong.

categories.name: Browser platform APIs
categories.description: Capabilities the browser itself provides, no framework required.

subcategories.name: Service workers & offline
subcategories.description: A proxy inside the browser that can answer requests when the network cannot.

subcategories.name: WebAssembly
subcategories.description: Runs compiled code in the page at near-native speed.

subcategories.name: Graphics
subcategories.description: Draws pixels, scenes, and shaders directly in the page.

subcategories.name: Media & devices
subcategories.description: Reaches the camera, microphone, files, and other hardware the reader consents to.

subcategories.name: Workers & background
subcategories.description: Moves heavy work off the main thread so the interface keeps responding.

categories.name: Content & commerce platforms
categories.description: Web apps you assemble rather than write from nothing.

subcategories.name: Traditional CMS
subcategories.description: Manages content and renders the site from the same system.

subcategories.name: Headless CMS
subcategories.description: Stores and edits content, then serves it over an API to any frontend.

subcategories.name: Site builders
subcategories.description: Builds and hosts a site visually, with no build step to run.

subcategories.name: E-commerce platforms
subcategories.description: Carts, catalogues, checkout, and order management, already written.

subcategories.name: Payments
subcategories.description: Takes money without the app ever touching a card number.

categories.name: Accessibility & reach
categories.description: Making the app usable by everyone, in the language and manner that suits them.

subcategories.name: Semantics & ARIA
subcategories.description: Uses the right element first, and ARIA only where HTML runs out.

subcategories.name: Keyboard & focus
subcategories.description: Every control reachable and visible without a pointer.

subcategories.name: Screen reader support
subcategories.description: What the page sounds like, tested on the readers people use.

subcategories.name: Internationalization
subcategories.description: Formats dates, numbers, and plurals for every locale the app serves.

subcategories.name: Localization workflow
subcategories.description: Gets strings to translators and translations back into the build.
